rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable angioedema from face swelling / Urgent priority evaluation
rule_level_problems.problem: The page's angioedema branch escalates to airway assessment and anaphylaxis management when there is airway obstruction (snoring, gurgling, noisy breathing). No finding for airway obstruction/stridor exists in any check list, and the anaphylaxis and priority rules only react to 'Sudden onset' face/tongue swelling plus a listed sign. Painless lip/eye swelling with noisy breathing is therefore recorded as a non-urgent probable Angioedema.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable sinusitis from face pain; Diagnose probable mumps from painful face swelling
rule_level_problems.problem: Both rules AND every descriptive feature of the flowchart box (sinusitis: face pain, tenderness, headache, thick/postnasal discharge, recent cold; mumps: swelling, pain, fever, headache, body pain). The page reads as a descriptive cluster, not a checklist; a strict conjunction will rarely fire. A patient with tender cheeks, headache and thick discharge but no reported recent cold gets no sinusitis diagnosis. Consider any2/any3 of the secondary features, or at least making 'recent common cold' and 'body pain' optional.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible stroke from face symptoms; Diagnose probable Bell's palsy
rule_level_problems.problem: Forehead sparing is expressed as (no Upper facial weakness), so an unrecorded forehead examination is treated as sparing and yields possible stroke/TIA. Also, Bell's palsy accepts 'Unable to close eyes' as evidence of forehead involvement, but the stroke rule excludes only 'Upper facial weakness', so sudden unilateral weakness + Unable to close eyes (forehead not recorded) fires both possible stroke and probable Bell's palsy. SNOMED's 'Lower facial weakness' (finding, child of Weakness of face muscles) would state forehead sparing as a positive finding.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable facial cellulitis; Diagnose probable orbital cellulitis; Diagnose probable mumps
rule_level_problems.problem: These probable rules use the unqualified finding (Swelling at Face structure), but every check_for in the file records it only with a qualifier (Sudden onset or New). Whether the 'probable evidence must be checked for in the same file' constraint accepts a qualified check for unqualified evidence could not be verified from the inputs allowed; if it does not, these rules fail the test. Likewise the mumps rule's (active_condition Fever) has no check_for in this file (Fever is a recorded common symptom, so this is probably accepted).

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable post-herpetic neuralgia of face
rule_level_problems.problem: 'History of herpes zoster' is not site-specific and cannot be side-matched to the pain, so the rule is looser than 'previous shingles on same side of face'.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable mumps from painful face swelling
rule_level_problems.problem: 'Body pain' is encoded as Generalized aches and pains; the recorded common symptom is Muscle pain, which is not a descendant, so a patient recorded with Muscle pain does not satisfy the clause.

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded: stroke/TIA (possible), anaphylaxis (possible), facial cellulitis, orbital cellulitis and kidney disease (probable), with an Urgent priority rule that follows the house pattern; every SNOMED concept resolves. The most consequential gap is outside the box: the angioedema branch's airway-obstruction escalation to anaphylaxis management has no finding or rule, so painless swelling with noisy breathing stays non-urgent. The sinusitis and mumps rules AND every descriptive feature and will under-fire; smaller losses are 'progressive', 'superficial', 'worse on bending forward', the shingles site/side and the allergen time window.
